analysis: Examined the three changed files. ProviderLoop+Testing.swift (head lines 514-523) adds two test seams: one sets selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride and one awaits the recovery task. The seams live in a non-#if DEBUG extension and are described as test-only. The override is a nil stored property in production, so a load-bypass needs in-process code execution (the TB-003 operator/process boundary), which is not a new remote attack surface. ProviderLoop.swift adds stored properties (selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride, savedEnabledModels, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch) at head lines ~724-735, plus the init assignment of savedEnabledModels at ~897. These are state only and carry no auth, crypto or network behavior. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift (head lines 50-51, 54) extends currentDaemonState() with enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. These are written to the local daemon state file via DaemonStateFile. The exposed data is model-id lists and a recovery report, which are already public through heartbeats and advertised models (per T-041/A-018 notes). No prompts, keys, tokens or attestation material are added. The DaemonStateFile permissions, the contents of selectedModelRecoveryReport(), the logic of the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery file, and how recovery loads interact with eviction, memory admission (T-029), the weight-hash check (T-027/T-012) and the hold socket (T-059) are not in the supplied evidence. The main open question for integration is whether recovery reloads go through ensureModelLoaded with the same weight-hash and verified-load checks. The diff gives no evidence that they do not. No concrete regressions identified in the supplied lines.
